title: Normalized derived pullback of a strict coefficient reduction tower
statement:
Let $f:(\mathscr X,R_X)\to(\mathscr Y,R_Y)$ be a morphism of ringed topoi presented by small sites, with a specified ring isomorphism $f^{-1}R_Y\cong R_X$. Module pullback $F=f^*$ is exact and left adjoint to module direct image $G=f_*$. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the ringed-topos convention [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism], and strict inverse sequences indexed by $\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}}$.
Let $Q_{Y,\bullet}$ be a strict tower of commutative $R_Y$-algebra sheaves with unital algebra transitions, and put $Q_{X,\bullet}=FQ_{Y,\bullet}$ with pulled-back structure maps. Write $\Delta_T$ for constant towers and $F^{\rm Tow}$ for exact termwise pullback. Set $B_T(K)=\Delta_TK\otimes^L_{\Delta_TR_T}Q_{T,\bullet}$ in the derived category of strict towers, equivalently the left derived functor of $P\mapsto(P\otimes_{R_T}Q_{T,n})_n$, with levels restricted to $R_T$. Its augmentation $i_{T,K}:\Delta_TK\to B_T(K)$ is induced by $R_T\to Q_{T,n}$.
There is a unique natural isomorphism
$$\tau_K:F^{\rm Tow}B_Y(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}B_X(FK)$$
whose component on every flat-term K-flat representative is the ordinary tensor/pullback comparison, conjugated by the universal reduction counits. The ordinary comparison is the inverse scalar-extension mate of the restriction/pullback comparison: on inverse-image pure tensors it sends $F(x\otimes q)$ to $F(x)\otimes F(q)$. It commutes with all coefficient transitions and satisfies $\tau_K F^{\rm Tow}(i_{Y,K})=i_{X,FK}$ under $F^{\rm Tow}\Delta_Y=\Delta_XF$. Its evaluations are the representative-normalized derived tensor/pullback comparisons. No perfectness or completeness is assumed.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal A_T=\operatorname{Mod}(R_T)$, $\mathcal T_T=\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A_T)$, and $q_T,q_T^{\rm Tow}$ for their homotopy-to-derived localizations. Define $a_T(P)=(P\otimes_{R_T}Q_{T,n})_n$, with transitions $1_P\otimes t_n$, where $t_n:Q_{T,n+1}\to Q_{T,n}$. This is an additive functor on complexes and homotopies. Kernels and cokernels in $\mathcal T_T$ are levelwise, so its cohomology is levelwise; hence a tower-complex map is a quasi-isomorphism exactly when every level is. The diagonal and termwise $F$ are exact since their evaluations are respectively the identity and the assumed exact $F$. Apply exact derived factorization to both. We use their canonical localization comparisons throughout, including $F^{\rm Tow}\Delta_Y\cong\Delta_XF$.

source.place: Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change; tower argument using levelwise kernels and cokernels

proof.text: Let $\mathcal P_T$ be the flat-term K-flat complexes. Every complex receives a quasi-isomorphism from one by K-flat resolution. If $s:P\to P'$ is a quasi-isomorphism between members of $\mathcal P_T$, apply the change-of-rings quasi-isomorphism theorem to $R_T\to Q_{T,n}$ at each $n$. Restricting scalars preserves its cohomology: restriction changes only the ring action, and kernels and sheafified cokernels retain the same underlying abelian sheaves. Thus every $s\otimes1_{Q_{T,n}}$ is a quasi-isomorphism of $R_T$-complexes. Step 1 now shows $a_T(s)$ is a quasi-isomorphism of whole strict tower complexes. No flatness of any $Q_{T,n}$ has been used.

source.place: Tags 06YS, lemma-K-flat-resolution, and 06YT, lemma-derived-tor-quasi-isomorphism-other-side; change of rings as in 06YY

proof.text: The homotopy functor $P\mapsto q_T^{\rm Tow}a_T(P)$ preserves shifts and cone triangles: tensor is additive, and at each level the cone differential is the same block matrix before and after tensoring. The resolving-class derived-functor criterion therefore applies using step 2. It gives the universal reduction counit $c_{T,P}:B_T(q_TP)\to q_T^{\rm Tow}a_T(P)$, invertible for every $P\in\mathcal P_T$. For a resolution $p:P\to K$, the normalized comparison at $K$ is $c_{T,P}\circ B_T(q_Tp)^{-1}$. This uses the definition of $B_T$ as the total left derived functor in the statement and fixes the counit, rather than selecting arbitrary model isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change, using Tag 06XN, derived.tex, lemma-find-existence-computes

proof.text: To check the alternative tensor description, realize strict towers on the small diagram site with $J=\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\rm op}$. Its coefficient sheaf is $\Delta R_T$, and $Q_{T,\bullet}$ is a commutative algebra sheaf on it. Level-$n$ evaluation is the module inverse image of the topos morphism $e_n$, with $e_n^{-1}\Delta R_T=R_T$. The canonical ringed tensor comparison for $e_n$, with identity coefficient map, therefore gives isomorphisms $\operatorname{ev}_n(M\otimes_{\Delta R_T}N)\cong M_n\otimes_{R_T}N_n$, natural in both modules and fixed by the generalized pure-tensor equation. Pure tensors commute with restrictions and determine maps out of the tensor. Both ways around the transition square therefore send $x\otimes y$ to $t(x)\otimes t(y)$, so these isomorphisms commute with the tower transitions. Thus diagram-site tensors are computed levelwise. For a flat-term K-flat $P$ and any acyclic tower complex $H$, evaluation of $\operatorname{Tot}(H\otimes\Delta P)$ is $\operatorname{Tot}(H_n\otimes P)$, which is acyclic; tower cohomology is levelwise, so $\Delta P$ is K-flat. Its terms are flat by the same levelwise exactness test. Since $\Delta$ is exact, $\Delta P\to\Delta K$ is a K-flat resolution. Apply derived change of rings on this ringed diagram site to $\Delta R_T\to Q_{T,\bullet}$ and then restrict scalars. By the levelwise computation, its value on $\Delta P$ is precisely $a_T(P)$ with transitions $1\otimes t_n$. Thus $\Delta K\otimes^L_{\Delta R_T}Q_{T,\bullet}$ has the model and normalization in step 3. This comparison takes place in the derived category of strict towers.

source.place: Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change, applied on the diagram site; K-flat computation

proof.text: Use the normalized ordinary ringed tensor comparison to define, for every module $M$ and every $n$, $\mu_{M,n}:F(M\otimes_{R_Y}Q_{Y,n})\xrightarrow{\sim}FM\otimes_{R_X}Q_{X,n}$. Its defining generalized pure-tensor equation is $F(m\otimes q)\mapsto Fm\otimes Fq$. The comparison exists naturally in both module variables by the cited construction; its pure tensors determine maps by the cited tensor section calculus. Here the structural ring map is the specified isomorphism $f^{-1}R_Y\cong R_X$, so all coefficient identifications are the specified ones, including $FQ_{Y,n}=Q_{X,n}$.

Check the mate normalization explicitly. Let $E_{T,n}$ be extension along $R_T\to Q_{T,n}$ and $\mathrm{Res}_{T,n}$ its right adjoint. Its unit is $m\mapsto m\otimes1$, using symmetry for the insertion convention of the tensor section calculus. Pullback on $R$-modules and on $Q_n$-modules is the same geometric inverse image with the indicated coefficient action, so the restriction/pullback comparison identifies their underlying inverse-image sections. The scalar-extension mate $E_{X,n}F\to F_{Q_n}E_{Y,n}$ is adjoint to this comparison composed with $F$ of the extension unit. On generators it is $Fm\otimes Fq\mapsto F(m\otimes1)\,Fq=F(m\otimes q)$. Its composite with $\mu_{M,n}$ in either order is the identity on pure tensors. Thus $\mu_{M,n}$ is its inverse after restriction, with exactly the direction asserted. This also gives $\mu_{M,n}F(m\mapsto m\otimes1)=(Fm\mapsto Fm\otimes1)$.

Naturality of $\mu$ in its second argument, applied to $t_n$, says $(1\otimes Ft_n)\mu_{M,n+1}=\mu_{M,n}F(1\otimes t_n)$. Thus the $\mu_{M,n}$ form an isomorphism of strict towers, with inverse also commuting with transitions. Apply it degree by degree to a complex $P$. Naturality in its first argument, applied to $d_P^r$, gives the cochain-map equation, and applied to any complex map or homotopy gives naturality on the homotopy category. Denote the resulting ordinary isomorphism by $\mu_P:F^{\rm Tow}a_Y(P)\xrightarrow{\sim}a_X(FP)$. This is a single map of tower complexes before localization, with all transitions retained.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, functoriality in both factors

proof.text:
If $P\in\mathcal P_Y$, then $FP\in\mathcal P_X$ by preservation of flat-term K-flat complexes under ringed pullback. Combine steps 3 and 7 to obtain on such representatives
$$\theta_P=c_{X,FP}^{-1}\circ q_X^{\rm Tow}(\mu_P)\circ F^{\rm Tow}(c_{Y,P}):F^{\rm Tow}B_Y(q_YP)\xrightarrow{\sim}B_X(F(q_YP)).$$
Exact-localization comparisons from step 1 are implicit in this typed formula. The equivalence $W_Y^{-1}\mathcal P_Y\simeq D(R_Y)$ in site-derived-tensor descent makes $q_Y|_{\mathcal P_Y}$ a localization. All arrows in the displayed formula are natural on $\mathcal P_Y$. The localization universal property extends $\theta$ and its inverse uniquely, giving a natural isomorphism $\tau$. Their composites descend the identity, so remain identities. Any natural transformation satisfying the prescribed representative equation restricts to $\theta$ and equals $\tau$ by the same fully faithful restriction. This proves existence, invertibility, naturality and the claimed uniqueness.

source.place: Tags 0G7E, lemma-pullback-K-flat, and 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change; descent through the resolving localization

proof.text:
Write $u_{T,P}:\Delta_TP\to a_T(P)$ for $p\mapsto(p\otimes1)_n$. Unitality of every $t_n$ makes this a map of strict tower complexes. The augmentation on representatives is $i_{T,q_TP}=c_{T,P}^{-1}q_T^{\rm Tow}(u_{T,P})$. This natural map on $\mathcal P_T$ extends uniquely through its localization, which is exactly the augmentation induced by $R_T\to Q_{T,n}$. Substituting step 8 and canceling $F^{\rm Tow}(c_{Y,P})$ gives
$$\theta_PF^{\rm Tow}(i_{Y,q_YP})=c_{X,FP}^{-1}q_X^{\rm Tow}(\mu_PF^{\rm Tow}(u_{Y,P}))=c_{X,FP}^{-1}q_X^{\rm Tow}(u_{X,FP})=i_{X,F(q_YP)}.$$
The middle equality is the unit calculation of step 6, already an equality of strict tower cochain maps. Localization uniqueness now proves the augmentation equation for every derived $K$.

source.place: Tags 03CZ and 03EL in sites-modules.tex, with Tag 06YY counit normalization

proof.text: Finally, exact evaluation sends $a_T(P)$ to $P\otimes Q_{T,n}$ and $\mu_P$ to $\mu_{P,n}$. The resolving-class criterion applied to the single-level functor gives its universal counit invertible on $\mathcal P_T$ by step 2. Consequently evaluation of $c_{T,P}$ identifies the tower reduction with this single-level derived reduction by their common localized representative model; the identification is unique by localization. Evaluating the formula of step 8 is therefore precisely the ordinary comparison $\mu_{P,n}$ conjugated by these single-level counits. The representative-normalized derived tensor/pullback comparison has this same formula; localization uniqueness identifies them for every $K$. Evaluation is used here to identify the stated evaluations, while the strict-tower map and its augmentation equality have already been constructed before evaluation. None of the arguments imposes perfection, boundedness, adic structure or completeness.
